messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate and DNS resolution timeouts observed for private endpoints in Azure westeurope (private-proxy-west-eu). 90th pct latency up, 5xx spike on proxy edge. Runbook: #runbooks/private-dns-routing. Link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/PR-42

eric: acked - I'm oncall. jumping in now. any obvious customer reports?

anna: seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN from private DNS zone. queries to our Azure Private DNS VA (10.10.2.3) sometimes return no-records for service.private.redwood.local and then succeed a few seconds later.

mike: graphs: https://metrics.internal/d/abcd123/proxy-west-eu - big spike in 502/504 starting ~5m ago. KV cache miss rate for west-eu increased x6 -> backend requests rose.

sara: pinging the private DNS VA and doing tcpdump on the interface to the expressroute. seeing bursts of UDP retransmits to 40053. not BGP flap. looks like DNS service side saturation/latency in the region.

eric: ok plan: (1) reduce customer impact by shifting routing for private-west-eu traffic to eu-central fallback, (2) clear problematic cached records we control, (3) keep customers updated. any objections?

anna: +1 for fallback. also we can rotate the Azure private DNS zone responders (swap primary to secondary) and purge our cache. I'll prep az commands.

mike: preparing the routing override and traffic-shift play. will do graceful 60/30/10 roll. will monitor 5xx and latency.

sara: what endpoint are we changing? is this just platform-internal? confirm no public endpoints.

eric: this affects Private (VPC/VNet) customers using ExpressRoute/Private Link into westeurope only. Hosted API unaffected.

anna: az CLI snippet if needed (will run from netops bastion):
```
az network private-dns record-set a remove-record --resource-group rg-dns-westeu --zone-name private.redwood.local --record-set-name service --ipv4-address 10.1.2.99
az network private-dns record-set a add-record --resource-group rg-dns-westeu --zone-name private.redwood.local --record-set-name service --ipv4-address 10.1.2.100
```

these are safe short swaps to nudge Azure resolver replication.

mike: routing override API call (internal control plane):
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"private-west-eu","action":"route-to","target":"eu-central","weight":60}'
```

eric: executing routing override now (will notify when traffic shifts).

deploy-bot: build/route-manager v3.14 invoked by eric - approval token present - starting gradual shift.

mike: override accepted by router. current distribution: west-eu 40% -> eu-central 60%. monitoring.

sara: running dig loop against internal resolver - intermittent NXDOMAIN rate down from ~25% to ~8% as we shift. good sign.

liz: drafting customer message for impacted Private customers: "We are experiencing intermittent connectivity to private endpoints in Azure West Europe affecting some Private-hosted connections. We have put in a temporary routing fallback to eu-central and are monitoring. We'll follow up with full impact once mitigated." anyone want to add specifics?

julia: please include the ETA for full mitigation (est 30-45m) and whether dedicated circuits (reserved capacity) were affected differently.

mike: AcmeCorp and BetaApps saw highest errors; both have expressroute circuits into westeurope. both are currently receiving traffic via eu-central fallback for control plane and proxy-ing.

eric: update: after 18m, 5xx rate reduced to baseline and tail latency improving. KV cache warmup in eu-central in progress - prewarmed 80%. still seeing occasional DNS misses in west-eu but non-impacting for shifted traffic.

anna: I'll continue with DNS zone responder rotation and run a propagation healthcheck script. if we still see churn after traffic returns, may need Azure SR.

sara: logs from proxy showing decreased backend timeouts. putting a temporary alert suppression for noisy alerts to avoid paging while we stabilize.

deploy-bot: route-manager v3.14: traffic shift completed to target weights. audit id: rm-202678.

eric: switching to handoff mode - netops will own remediation, oncall will monitor for 2 hours then sign off. @anna take lead for root cause and SR engagement if required.

anna: taking lead. starting SR draft to Azure with timed traces and packet captures. attaching sb pcap id: pc-78921.

liz: sent initial customer note to impacted customers (AcmeCorp, BetaApps) and created support tickets. will post copy in #customer-commms for signoff.

julia: post-incident ask: timeline, customer impact table, and whether our smart-routing can auto-failback when DNS health is consistent. add to action items.

eric: marking thread as mitigated -> status: mitigation in place, customers rerouted to eu-central. handoff to netops for RCA and Azure SR. will open incident postmortem ticket.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident ID INC-2026-4821. Pager cleared at 1781237890.

eric: thanks everyone. please add findings to the postmortem template and include any runbook gaps (DNS responder rotation steps should be in runbook). I'll loop back in retrospective. :thumbsup:
